    names_to = "Sample",
    values_to = "CPM"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CPM_log2 = log2(CPM + 1))

gil16_annotation <- annotation %>%
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^GIL16", Gene_ID)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Gene_number = as.numeric(sub(".*_(\\d+)$", "\\1", Gene_ID)),
    Color = dplyr::case_when(
      Strand == "+" & !is.na(Gene_number) & Gene_number >= 1 & Gene_number <= 8  ~ "red",
      Strand == "+" & !is.na(Gene_number) & Gene_number >= 9 & Gene_number <= 30 ~ "darkred",
      Strand == "+" & !is.na(Gene_number) & Gene_number >= 33 & Gene_number <= 36 ~ "grey",
      Strand == "-" ~ "blue",
      TRUE ~ "black"
    )
  )

gil16_long_cpm <- gil16_long_cpm %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    gil16_annotation %>%
      dplyr::select(Gene_ID, Color, Gene_symbol, Description, Subtype),
    by = "Gene_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Gene_symbol = ifelse(is.na(Gene_symbol), "", Gene_symbol),
    Description = ifelse(is.na(Description), "", Description),
    Subtype = ifelse(is.na(Subtype), "-", Subtype),
    Gene_ID = factor(
      Gene_ID,
      levels = gil16_annotation$Gene_ID[
        gil16_annotation$Gene_ID %in% Gene_ID
      ]
    )
  )

p <- ggplot(gil16_long_cpm, aes(
  x = Gene_ID,
  y = CPM_log2,
  text = paste(
    "Gene ID:", Gene_ID,
    ifelse(
      Gene_symbol != "",
      paste0("<br>Gene symbol: ", Gene_symbol),
      ""
    ),
    ifelse(
      Description != "",
      paste0("<br>Description: ", Description),
      ""
    ),
    ifelse(
      Description == "Hypothetical protein",
      paste0("<br>Phynteny annotation: ", Subtype),
      ""
    ),
    "<br>Sample:", Sample,
    "<br>Gene expression:", round(CPM_log2, 2)
  )
)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.25,
    size = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.7,
    aes(color = Color)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab("Gene expression") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, ceiling(max(gil16_long_cpm$CPM_log2, na.rm = TRUE)))) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

title: Time points 10 vs 0 contrast
text:
In order to perform the time 10 vs 0 contrast, we established a log₂ fold-change (LFC) threshold of ±0.585. This value reflects an increase or decrease in expression of 50%, depending on whether it is positive or negative, respectively. The default value is 0, but when performing the other contrasts we obtained too many differentially expressed (DE) genes. This violates one of DESeq2’s key assumptions, which is that most genes are not differentially expressed.
Code
contrast <- results(dds, contrast = list(c("Time_10_vs_0", "MMC_TRUE_vs_FALSE")), lfcThreshold = log2(1.5))
contrast_df <- as.data.frame(contrast)

contrast_df <- contrast_df %>%
  { x <- .; x$Gene_ID <- rownames(x); x } %>%
  left_join(
    annotation %>%
      filter(Gene_ID %in% rownames(contrast_df)) %>%
      dplyr::select(Gene_ID, Gene_symbol, Description, COG, Classification, Association, Type, Subtype, Source),
    by = "Gene_ID"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Mean_normalized_counts = baseMean,
    LFC = log2FoldChange,
    Adjusted_p_value = padj
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Gene_ID,
    Gene_symbol,
    Description,
    COG,
    Classification,
    Association,
    Type,
    Subtype,
    Source,
    Mean_normalized_counts,
    LFC,
    Adjusted_p_value
  )
As can be seen in the summary() results, 20 upregulated and 7 downregulated genes were obtained. In addition, 484 genes were discarded due to low counts, likely because they are expressed in latter times or in the presence of GIL01 or GIL16. Below is an interactive table where all DE genes can be viewed individually.

title: Time points 60 vs 0 contrast
text:
In order to perform the time 60 vs 0 contrast, we established a log₂ fold-change (LFC) threshold of ±0.585. This value reflects an increase or decrease in expression of 50%, depending on whether it is positive or negative, respectively. The default value is 0, but when performing the other contrasts we obtained too many differentially expressed (DE) genes. This violates one of DESeq2’s key assumptions, which is that most genes are not differentially expressed.
Code
contrast <- results(dds, contrast = list(c("Time_60_vs_0", "MMC_TRUE_vs_FALSE")), lfcThreshold = log2(1.5))
contrast_df <- as.data.frame(contrast)

contrast_df <- contrast_df %>%
  { x <- .; x$Gene_ID <- rownames(x); x } %>%
  left_join(
    annotation %>%
      filter(Gene_ID %in% rownames(contrast_df)) %>%
      dplyr::select(Gene_ID, Gene_symbol, Description, COG, Classification, Association, Type, Subtype, Source),
    by = "Gene_ID"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Mean_normalized_counts = baseMean,
    LFC = log2FoldChange,
    Adjusted_p_value = padj
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Gene_ID,
    Gene_symbol,
    Description,
    COG,
    Classification,
    Association,
    Type,
    Subtype,
    Source,
    Mean_normalized_counts,
    LFC,
    Adjusted_p_value
  )

title: Time points 60-mock vs 0 contrast
text:
In order to perform the time 60-mock vs 0 contrast, we established a log₂ fold-change (LFC) threshold of ±0.585. This value reflects an increase or decrease in expression of 50%, depending on whether it is positive or negative, respectively. The default value is 0, but when performing the other contrasts we obtained too many differentially expressed (DE) genes. This violates one of DESeq2’s key assumptions, which is that most genes are not differentially expressed.
Code
contrast <- results(dds, contrast = c("Time", "60", "0"), lfcThreshold = log2(1.5))
contrast_df <- as.data.frame(contrast)

contrast_df <- contrast_df %>%
  { x <- .; x$Gene_ID <- rownames(x); x } %>%
  left_join(
    annotation %>%
      filter(Gene_ID %in% rownames(contrast_df)) %>%
      dplyr::select(Gene_ID, Gene_symbol, Description, COG, Classification, Association, Type, Subtype, Source),
    by = "Gene_ID"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Mean_normalized_counts = baseMean,
    LFC = log2FoldChange,
    Adjusted_p_value = padj
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Gene_ID,
    Gene_symbol,
    Description,
    COG,
    Classification,
    Association,
    Type,
    Subtype,
    Source,
    Mean_normalized_counts,
    LFC,
    Adjusted_p_value
  )
As can be seen in the summary() results, 249 upregulated and 210 downregulated genes were obtained. In addition, 294 genes were discarded due to low counts, probably because they are expressed in inducted samples or in the absence of GIL01. Below is an interactive table where all DE genes can be viewed individually.

title: Time points 30 vs 0 contrast
text:
In order to perform the time 30 vs 0 contrast, we established a log₂ fold-change (LFC) threshold of ±0.585. This value reflects an increase or decrease in expression of 50%, depending on whether it is positive or negative, respectively. The default value is 0, but when performing the other contrasts we obtained too many differentially expressed (DE) genes. This violates one of DESeq2’s key assumptions, which is that most genes are not differentially expressed.
Code
contrast <- results(dds, contrast = list(c("Time_30_vs_0", "MMC_TRUE_vs_FALSE")), lfcThreshold = log2(1.5))
contrast_df <- as.data.frame(contrast)

contrast_df <- contrast_df %>%
  { x <- .; x$Gene_ID <- rownames(x); x } %>%
  left_join(
    annotation %>%
      filter(Gene_ID %in% rownames(contrast_df)) %>%
      dplyr::select(Gene_ID, Gene_symbol, Description, COG, Classification, Association, Type, Subtype, Source),
    by = "Gene_ID"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Mean_normalized_counts = baseMean,
    LFC = log2FoldChange,
    Adjusted_p_value = padj
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Gene_ID,
    Gene_symbol,
    Description,
    COG,
    Classification,
    Association,
    Type,
    Subtype,
    Source,
    Mean_normalized_counts,
    LFC,
    Adjusted_p_value
  )
As can be seen in the summary() results, 284 upregulated and 312 downregulated genes were obtained. In addition, 294 genes were discarded due to low counts, probably because they are expressed in latter times or in the absence of GIL16. title: Time points 60 vs 60-mock contrast
text:
In order to perform the time 60 vs 60-mock contrast, we established a log₂ fold-change (LFC) threshold of ±0.585. This value reflects an increase or decrease in expression of 50%, depending on whether it is positive or negative, respectively. The default value is 0, but when performing the other contrasts we obtained too many differentially expressed (DE) genes. This violates one of DESeq2’s key assumptions, which is that most genes are not differentially expressed.
Code
contrast <- results(dds, name = "MMC_TRUE_vs_FALSE", lfcThreshold = log2(1.5))
contrast_df <- as.data.frame(contrast)

contrast_df <- contrast_df %>%
  { x <- .; x$Gene_ID <- rownames(x); x } %>%
  left_join(
    annotation %>%
      filter(Gene_ID %in% rownames(contrast_df)) %>%
      dplyr::select(Gene_ID, Gene_symbol, Description, COG, Classification, Association, Type, Subtype, Source),
    by = "Gene_ID"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Mean_normalized_counts = baseMean,
    LFC = log2FoldChange,
    Adjusted_p_value = padj
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Gene_ID,
    Gene_symbol,
    Description,
    COG,
    Classification,
    Association,
    Type,
    Subtype,
    Source,
    Mean_normalized_counts,
    LFC,
    Adjusted_p_value
  )

title: Results summary
text:
Venn diagrams
Venn diagrams were used to evaluate the overlap of differentially expressed genes associated with lysogeny among the three pairwise strain comparisons. Separate analyses were performed for upregulated and downregulated genes. Each circle represents the set of genes showing differential expression in a given strain comparison, whereas overlapping regions indicate genes shared between two or more comparisons. Genes located in the intersections correspond to transcriptional differences that are common across strain contrasts, while genes found exclusively in a single region represent comparison-specific responses. This analysis facilitates the identification of both conserved and unique transcriptional signatures associated with lysogeny and provides an overview of the extent to which differential gene expression patterns are shared among strains.

text:
Upset plots
Upset plots were used to examine the overlap of DE genes among pairwise strain comparisons performed at different time points (30, 60 and 60-mock). Separate analyses were conducted for upregulated (in red) and downregulated (in blue) genes. Each set represents the genes identified in a specific strain comparison at a given time point, whereas intersections correspond to genes shared across multiple pairwise comparisons. title: Results summary
text:
Barplots
This plot shows the number of DE genes, both upregulated and downregulated, in each contrast per strain. As we can see, there doesn’t appear to be a difference in the number of DE genes according to the strain. This is because three independent models (i.e. three DESeq2 objects) were constructed for each set of contrasts, reflecting that the contrasts with fewer DE genes are those from early time points (0 and 10 minutes), while those performed with late time points (60 or 60-mock) show a large number of DE genes.

This plot shows the number of enrichments found in each category. Most enrichments are found in the BP GO category, unlike what happened in lysogeny, which were mainly found in MF and CC. In this plot, the contrasts between GBJ002 time points show less enrichments than with GIL01 or GIL16, which would reflect the differences found in gene expression throughout MMC induction (even without induction) when any of these tectiviruses are present.

title: Results summary
text:
Upset plots
Upset plots were used to evaluate the overlap of DE genes across the temporal contrasts analyzed within each strain (GBJ002, GIL01 and GIL16). Each set corresponds to the genes identified as significantly upregulated (in red) or downregulated (in blue) in a specific contrast and intersections represent genes shared among two or more contrasts. The size of each intersection reflects the number of genes exhibiting a common transcriptional response across the corresponding comparisons, whereas the set size indicates the total number of DE genes detected in each contrast. This analysis enables the identification of genes specifically associated with individual stages of the experiment as well as genes displaying persistent transcriptional changes across multiple time points, thereby providing insights into the dynamics and conservation of the transcriptional response within each strain.

  "Time points 10 vs 0",
  "Time points 30 vs 0",

  "Time points 60-mock vs 0"
